A Laredo jury has convicted U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) officer Eliomar Santos on all four counts against him in an assault case stemming from a 2022 incident at a fellow officer's home in Laredo, according to KGNS.

The jury returned the guilty verdict on Thursday, Nov. 6. One of the four counts is a third-degree felony, according to KGNS, which did not specify which count carries the felony charge. The other counts are assault causing bodily injury, unlawful restraint, and interference with an emergency request for assistance.

Prosecutors said Santos assaulted a fellow CBP officer, a woman, at her home in 2022. According to KGNS, prosecutors said Santos handcuffed the woman, held her in a closet, and prevented her from calling for help. Webb Watch 956 is not naming the woman, who was not named in the KGNS report.

Santos' attorneys argued he was acting in self-defense and asked the jury to acquit him, according to KGNS. The jury rejected that argument.

Update — Friday, Nov. 6, 7:51 p.m.: The Webb & Zapata County District Attorney's Office has announced the sentence. The jury assessed three years' probation for the third-degree felony count of assault family violence impeding breath, and one year in the Texas Department of Criminal Justice for the assault, unlawful restraint and interference with an emergency call counts. The trial, before 406th District Court Judge David E. Garcia, lasted five days, and the jury deliberated about an hour and a half before returning the guilty verdicts.

Sources: KGNS; Webb & Zapata County District Attorney's Office (Facebook post, Nov. 6, 2026).

title: Laredo Jury Convicts CBP Officer Eliomar Santos on All Four Counts in Assault Case
